one_side: human use; hum use; human medicine; in humans; in hum
other_side: veterinary use; vet use; veterinary medicine; veterinary medecine; vet medicine; vet med; in animals; in animal
why_it_matters: Goods for human use and goods for veterinary use are different commodities and are classified apart. The marker must be the stated USE, not the word human on its own: 22 descriptions say human blood or of human origin, which is a material and not a purpose, and a bare human marker read those as human-use. That is how 3002.90.10 and 3002.90.20 came to be offered as each other's successor. The same trap sits on the animal side and was missed when the human side was fixed: 36 descriptions say animal blood, of animal origin or human or animal substances, which is a material, while only 2 say for use in animals or for administration in animal, which is a purpose. Bare animal would have read the material as veterinary, so only the purpose forms are markers.
known_exceptions: Descriptions naming both, such as gel preparations for human/vet medicine, carry each marker and correctly fail to separate. Wordings taken from the corpus on 2026-08-11, including the abbreviation vet use and the misspelling veterinary medecine, neither of which the earlier marker veterinary could match. Animal purpose wordings taken from the corpus 2026-08-11: in animals and in animal, matching the human side's in humans and in hum.

why_it_matters: Whether a product is packaged for sale to the public decides which code it gets. Written short these are 'frs' and 'nfrs': one letter apart, opposite meanings. This is the clearest case where the matching score cannot see the thing that decides the answer.

This separates two whole headings, not two sub-codes. Heading 3003 is medicine that is not measured into doses. Heading 3004 is medicine that is. Two products on opposite sides of this sit in different headings and are not the same thing.
Whether the material came from people or from animals. This describes the source material rather than who the product is for.
known_exceptions: Family IM_0051. At the 1998 revision the human-origin and animal-origin dried blood codes were both retired and replaced by one code, whose description still mentions only animal origin.

why_it_matters: Immunological products are separated by whether they have been modified. This is here mainly to protect code 3002.10.00.60, worth 1.58 billion dollars, which is the one routing still waiting on expert confirmation.
known_exceptions: Wording such as 'whether or not modified' means either one, so it is not treated as a conflict.

why_it_matters: Whether the product was made using biotechnology. Weak on its own, because most descriptions say 'whether or not obtained by biotechnological processes', which means either one. Kept because it costs nothing to check.

corpus_coverage_2026_08_10: 5 one side / 0 other side of 572; ONE-SIDED, cannot fire on this delivery
why_it_matters: Sterile surgical materials are separated from non-sterile ones. In this delivery the contrast is carried by the subheading rather than by opposed wording: all 5 mentions are affirmative and all sit in 3006.10, which the Harmonized System defines as sterile surgical goods. Non-sterile equivalents are classified outside Chapter 30, so no description here can state the other side. A phrase pair cannot capture a distinction the nomenclature carries structurally, and that is why this rule reads as one-sided rather than as broken.
known_exceptions: Corrected 2026-08-10. The denial list held only 'non-sterile', so 'not sterile' and 'other than sterile' both returned not mentioned instead of the other side, and the rule would have stayed silent rather than firing. No description in this delivery uses any of the three, so the correction changes no current result and closes a path by which the rule could fail without saying so.

one_side: same content words with different punctuation or spacing
other_side: same content words with the same punctuation
why_it_matters: The inverse of a decisive distinction, recorded so the rule is stated rather than assumed. Statistics Canada rewrote punctuation without changing the goods. 25 import commodities are held under two strings each, 50 records worth CAD 42,982,705,212, and 21 of the pairs split at exactly 2002-01. A difference of this kind must never veto a link. Stage 0 missed 3 of the 25 groups until 2026-08-10, worth CAD 11,472,590,012: 3004900074 at CAD 10,243,535,741, 3004900076 at CAD 912,743,486 and 3005900040 at CAD 316,310,785. Its grouping key kept the spaces left behind by removed punctuation, so it could not see a space that had moved. Exports have no such pairs.
known_exceptions: 3005900040 swaps the connector, writing 'Dressings/sim art' against 'Dressings & sim art'. Both sides still read 'o/t of cotton', so it is a connector change and not a cotton distinction. Whether a twin pair is one commodity or two is a judgement for Stage 1, and this row records only that punctuation alone cannot settle it. Status is non_decisive so the checker skips the row, which reads active rows only.

why_it_matters: Whether a medicament contains an antibiotic decides its code inside heading 3004. The two wordings differ by one word and name products the tariff deliberately keeps apart.

Whether the product is a mixture. This pair is one of the two reasons the matcher gained word boundaries on 2026-08-10: 'unmixed' contains 'mixed' as a substring, so a plain search read every denial as the assertion.
known_exceptions: Wording such as 'whether or not mixed' means either one, so it is not treated as a conflict.

why_it_matters: A product given to prevent disease is not a product used to detect it. Diagnostic reagents administered to the patient sit in heading 3006, while prophylactic preparations sit in 3002 and 3004.

other_side: other than cotton;other than of cotton;o/t of cotton
why_it_matters: Dressings of woven fabric are split by whether the fabric is solely cotton. Commodity 3005900040 is not an instance: both of its descriptions read 'o/t of cotton', so that pair is a connector change and not this distinction.
known_exceptions: Corrected 2026-08-10 after running against the delivery. Shorthand expansion turns 'o/t of cotton' into 'other than of cotton', and neither original phrase matched that, so the rule could not fire on any of the 3 descriptions carrying it. 3005900040 is still not an instance: both its descriptions read other than cotton.

corpus_coverage_2026_08_10: 6 one side / 3 other side of 572; CANNOT FIRE on this delivery, and the counts do not show it: all 3 knit wordings ALSO say woven, being the same dressings line covering both, so no string sits on the knit side alone. Counting each side separately cannot express this. Finding 136, 2026-08-18.
why_it_matters: Woven and knitted fabrics are separated within subheading 3005.90. The two words share almost no letters, yet the descriptions around them are otherwise identical, so text similarity scores such a pair as a near-perfect match.
known_exceptions: Corrected 2026-08-10. The delivery writes 'knit fab', which expands to 'knit fabric' and never to 'knitted', so the original phrase matched none of the 3 descriptions. 'non-woven' denies woven correctly, because non is a reversing word.

why_it_matters: Two controlled precursors with different codes and different regulatory treatment. Corrected 2026-08-10: the contrast was written as ephedrine against pseudoephedrine, and bare ephedrine appears in no description in the delivery. What the data actually separates is pseudoephedrine from norephedrine, 4 descriptions against 4.
known_exceptions: Word boundaries are what keep these apart, since norephedrine and pseudoephedrine both contain ephedrine as a substring.

why_it_matters: One side carries a residual marker applied to a phrase the other states plainly, so the two name mutually exclusive sets and cannot be the same goods. 3002410010 'against influenza virus' against 3002410090 'o/t against influenza virus' score 0.922 as text.
known_exceptions: Fires only when exactly one side is residual. Two residual baskets are not complements, and a residual marker applied to different goods is not either.

why_it_matters: Both descriptions are lists and one item set is a proper subset of the other. 3002900019 'Toxins, toxoids, antitoxins' against 3002900020 'Toxoids, antitoxins'.
known_exceptions: The action is review rather than disqualify because losing an item from a list does not make the lineage wrong. It needs a person. This is workbook row 16.

why_it_matters: Two descriptions share their frame and differ in the single term that carries the meaning. The similarity score measures the frame, so these rank high while naming different goods: waste pharmaceuticals of heading 30.03 against heading 30.01 scores 0.9804, Lincomycin against Vancomycin 0.9412, anti-infective against antineoplastic 0.8667, which is above the automatic-link threshold.
known_exceptions: Review, never disqualify. Tested against Canada's concordance the shape fires on 5 of 125 known-correct successions and four are ordinary restylings, such as Anaesthetic for veterinary use becoming Other medicaments for veterinary use nes. Removing candidates at that error rate would repeat the specific_vs_residual mistake. The row is flagged and no recommendation is made. TWO KNOWN MISSES, left uncaught on purpose. 3006.80.90.43 'Waste pharmaceuticals of the goods of subheading 3004.90' against 'heading 30.01' at 0.9159, and 3006.80.19.00 'Waste of gel prep' against 'Gel prep' at 0.8645, CAD 205,645 between them. Catching both needs the unique-word allowance raised from 4 to 7, which flags 17 of Canada's 125 known-correct successions instead of 5 and raises corpus flags from 453 to 806. Tripling the noise on every other row is not worth those two, and both are visible to a reader because the queue prints both descriptions.
